title: Maro Itoje: Saracens in talks with England captain as Top 14 clubs circle
article_text:
Saracens are hopeful of extending Maro Itoje's deal amid reported interest from Top 14 clubs, which could spell the end of the England captain's Test career.

Discussions are under way to extend Itoje's Saracens stay beyond its current expiry after next year's Rugby World Cup.

However, the second row will be 33 by the end of the tournament and faces potentially his final chance to take up longstanding interest in him from across the Channel.

Any move to France would put Itoje's Test career on hold, with the Rugby Football Union having a policy of not selecting overseas-based players.

French newspaper Midi-Olympique claims European champions Bordeaux-Begles and Perpignan are among those to have been alerted to Itoje's potential availability, external.

While Saracens are optimistic of reaching a new agreement with Itoje, they are aware they are competing with Top 14 clubs with more spending power.

The headline salary cap in the French top flight stands at 11m euros (£9.2m), which is significantly higher than the Prem's equivalent figure of £6.4m.

The Top 14 also benefits from a more lucrative broadcast deal than its English equivalent, with a blockbuster five-year agreement with Canal Plus coming into effect from next season, external.

However, unlike in France, the English top flight allows one player at each club to sit outside the salary cap, in a so-called marquee spot, which may give Saracens more freedom to compete with overseas offers.

By staying in England, Itoje would also be eligible for a central England contract, worth about £150,000 a year.

As part of an agreement between clubs and country, Itoje was rested for England's summer fixtures against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina after several seasons of heavy workload.

While a move to the Top 14 would remove international fixtures from Itoje's schedule, French top-flight rugby is arduous.

As well as each club having 26 regular-season fixtures, the top six also qualify for the Top 14's post-season play-offs, with European fixtures on top.

Itoje has been at Saracens since he was a teenager, staying during their single season in the second-tier Championship after their punishment for repeated breaches of the salary cap.

Paris-based Racing 92 have been credited with an interest in Itoje in the past, without a move transpiring.

England's policy of only picking players from domestic rugby – a key protection for the domestic game - has come under pressure recently.

Jack Willis, who represented England at the 2023 Rugby World Cup, has enjoyed a stellar stint at Toulouse, winning the Top 14's player of the season award in each of the past two campaigns.

Former England captain Courtney Lawes, who has returned to the Prem and Sale after two seasons with Brive, has said he believes the bar should be scrapped. Ellis Genge, part of England's current leadership group, has also advocated a change, external.

The end of a Rugby World Cup cycle can be a convenient time for players to make a move abroad.

Willis was joined by fellow England internationals Joe Marchant and David Ribbans in the Top 14 immediately after the 2023 tournament while Lawes, Lewis Ludlam, Kyle Sinckler, Owen Farrell, Manu Tuilagi, Jonny May and Billy Vunipola made moves to France in the following summer.

title: Kildunne drops to bench as Red Roses ring changes
article_text:
Star full-back Ellie Kildunne has been dropped to the bench as England shake up their selection in response to a first defeat in four years.

Kildunne was part of the starting XV who lost 24-21 to Canada last Friday in Toronto with the Red Roses' unbeaten streak ending at 41 matches.

Head coach John Mitchell has accused his side of losing the hunger that fuelled a run which took in four successive Six Nations Grand Slams and last year's landmark world title on home soil.

"Last Friday, we lost sight of what we could control when it mattered most. That's on us to fix," said Mitchell.

"This week is about getting back to who we are - hungry, accountable to each other and demanding more of ourselves than anyone outside this group ever could."

Emma Sing comes in at full-back in Kildunne's place for Saturday's rematch (00:00 BST) against Canada in Ottawa, while Tatyana Heard and Claudia Moloney-MacDonald - backline starters in the defeat - drop out of the matchday squad entirely.

Helena Rowland and Mia Venner replace Heard and Moloney-MacDonald at inside centre and wing respectively.

In the fourth change to the starting line-up, Sadia Kabeya, who appeared off the bench last week on her comeback from a leg injury, starts with Alex Matthews, two-time Rugby World Cup winner, dropping to the bench.

Exeter's Flo Robinson and Sale's Hollie Aitchison are included on the bench as a new-look set of half-back replacements.

Sing, a rangy runner who can also kick goals, started two matches at full-back during England's Six Nations campaign, with Kildunne switching to a different position on the wing on each occasion.

Sing's Gloucester-Hartpury team-mate Venner made her England debut in 2020 aged just 17.

Venner has won only another four caps since but was putting pressure on England's more established back three at the start of this year, appearing in wins over Scotland and Italy.

The 24-year-old finished as the PWR's joint top try-scorer last season, crossing 12 times.

Moloney-MacDonald cost her side an early try in the defeat by Canada when, after doing superbly to pick Jess Breach's pass off her toes, she spilled the ball over the line in the sixth minute.

"We've earned a strong period but nothing about it is owed to us going forward," said Mitchell.

"Friday [Saturday 00:00 BST] is an opportunity to apply sustained pressure, learn from what we missed and come out the other side better than we went in."

title: Audit regulator takes control of inquiry into Man City accounts
Boulter wins in under an hour to reach quarters
article_text:
Katie Boulter moved into the quarter-finals of the Japan Open after she beat Viktorija Golubic in less than an hour.

The British number two defeated her Swiss opponent 6-2 6-1 in Osaka and will face either Croatia's Antonia Ruzic or American Kayla Day in the next round.

Boulter saved a break point in the opening game but dominated from 2-2 in the first set, winning nine games in a row before Golubic took the penultimate game of the match.

The 30-year-old lost the British number one spot to Sonny Kartal on Monday, but is set to retake the position following her run this week.

Boulter, who is seeded eighth in the competition, said she was pleased with how she handled "difficult conditions", with a strong wind affecting play.

"I think one of the biggest things for me is staying patient in the wind," she said.

"Sometimes I can get a little frustrated, and I'm very pleased that I didn't allow that to affect me today and I think I ended up playing some really good tennis in the second set. I'm really pleased with the performance."

title: Ellie Kildunne has been dropped by England – here's why
article_text:
England head coach John Mitchell has dropped Ellie Kildunne to the bench for the Red Roses' clash with Canada in Ottawa.

The shock call comes after England suffered their first defeat in four years.

Canada ended the Red Roses' stunning 41-match unbeaten run with a narrow win in Toronto.

Mitchell has now made four changes to his starting XV as England look to bounce back.

Gloucester-Hartpury star Emma Sing takes over at full-back, while Mia Venner comes in on the wing.

Helena Rowland returns at inside centre, with Sadia Kabeya the only change to the pack.

Kildunne, one of England's biggest stars, has been named among the replacements.

Mitchell has not confirmed why Kildunne has lost her starting place.

However, some England fans believe the decision could be down to the balance of the backline.

Sing is a specialist full-back, and her selection has been welcomed by supporters who want to see England try a different approach.

Another supporter, Darren Mills, welcomed the change at full-back.

"A FB at FB, now thats a novelty," he wrote.

The comments suggest some fans believe Sing could offer England a better balance in the back three.

However, that remains a theory among supporters rather than an official reason given by Mitchell.

Not everyone agrees with the decision to leave Kildunne on the bench.

Steven Gardiner questioned the call, writing: "Kildunne dropped !? Isn't she our best player"

Guy Williamson felt the England star should have kept her place in a different role.

Was John Mitchell right to drop Ellie Kildunne to the bench?

Ellie Kildunne is one of the biggest stars in women's rugby, but there is plenty fans might not know about her.

From her rugby-playing brother to tattooing her England coach, here are six surprising facts.

1. Her younger brother is also a rugby star

Rugby talent runs in the Kildunne family.

Ellie's younger brother, Sam Kildunne, joined Doncaster Knights from Ampthill in August 2026.

The winger has also played sevens for England and Great Britain.

Ellie has spoken about her dream of competing at the Olympics alongside her brother.

Kildunne bought a £30 tattoo gun online and decided to try tattooing.

She started by practising on herself before finding other willing volunteers.

One of them was England head coach John Mitchell, who let her tattoo him after the 2025 Rugby World Cup.

Kildunne was chosen for Mattel's Team Barbie campaign.

She joined rugby stars Ilona Maher, Portia Woodman-Wickliffe and Nassira Konde in the project.

The campaign aimed to inspire young girls and help them build confidence.

Despite growing up in Yorkshire, Kildunne has always supported Liverpool.

Her childhood heroes included Steven Gerrard and Fernando Torres.

She even played football for Farsley Celtic, whose youth team once beat Manchester City's academy side 7-1.

5. She has tattoos dedicated to her family

Kildunne has small dots tattooed on her fingers to represent her parents and younger brother.

She explained that the tattoos help her feel close to her family wherever she goes.

The England star also has a passion for photography and owns several cameras.

6. She wrote 6,000 words about an Olympic legend

Kildunne once turned a simple school typing task into a huge project.

Asked to complete an exercise, she chose to write about Olympic champion Jessica Ennis-Hill.

She ended up producing more than 6,000 words.

title: Another major champion set for LIV exit
article_text:
With LIV Golf’s future shrouded in doubt despite BC Partners’ pledge to invest, another major champion has declared himself out of whatever form the league continues in.

Jon Rahm has already ruled himself out of being a LIV player next season, and Sergio Garcia has had his contract terminated in the courts though could still re-sign before the start of next season. Brooks Koepka and Patrick Reed left before the start of the 2026 season, meaning that a total of seven major championship wins had already made their way to the exit.

And now Louis Oosthuizen looks set to make it eight.

The 2010 Open champion is in Hong Kong for the Asian Tour’s Link Hong Kong Open and he told the South China Morning Post that he has no plans to continue playing in LIV 2.0 should it get off the ground as he expects that the travel schedule will be too much for the 44-year-old’s body.

It is “a lot of international travel for single events,” the South African said.

“I need to arrange my own schedule and look after my body. I want to play near one spot for three weeks at a time, not have all the big traveling for one tournament.

“I loved LIV and the team aspect, but it’s time to move on.”

Shortly afterwards, Oosthuizen released an official statement on Instagram confirming what he’d already suggested.

of the best decisions of my life, moving away from the traditional golf world and into something very special with LIV Golf and Southern Guards GC [formerly Stinger GC],” Oosthuizen said.

“I’m the biggest supporter of team golf and always will be. Golf needs more of it…

“I realised I have a lot more in me, and my biggest fear was that the schedule on LIV 2.0 would be tough to manage.

“This is probably the hardest decision I’ve had to make in my career, but I have to do what I believe is right for my golf.”

Oosthuizen won his only major title at St Andrews in 2010, and has completed a Career Grand Slam of runner-up finishes at each of the four major championships, but he’ll return to the Home of Golf for the 2027 Open having started the year competing on the DP World Tour in events co-sanctioned with the Sunshine Tour in South Africa.

title: Stormers appeal Investec Champions Cup ban decision
article_text:
DHL Stormers are disputing the three-match ban handed to hooker JJ Kotze for the 20-minute red card he received against Bristol in the opening round of the Champions Cup.

Kotze was sent off by French referee Kevin Bralley in the 33rd minute of the match for a dangerous, head-on-head tackle on Bears scrum-half, Kieran Marmion, which contravened Law 9.13.

Despite the loss of Kotze, the Stormers opened their campaign with a thumping 49-12 win over their callow opponents, Springbok star Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu converting all seven of their tries, which included braces for reported Irish target Jonathan Roche and Leolin Zas.

The Foul Play Review Committee determined that Kotze’s indiscretion warranted a three-match ban, but that sanction was not accepted by the Pool 3 leaders and a disciplinary hearing will now take place on Wednesday.

Meanwhile, Toulouse have accepted the three-match ban issued to prop Rodrigue Neti for the red card he received in the 15th minute of Les Rouge et Noir’s 43-40 win at home to Exeter Chiefs.

Neti was given his marching orders by referee Hollie Davidson for a dangerous tackle on Chiefs back-rower Ross Vintcent.

He will be free to play agaion on 9 November but that date will be brought forward by a week if he successfully completes the World Rugby Coaching intervention programme.

title: Upsets and dramatic finishes on opening day of French Open 2026
article_text:
The YONEX French Open 2026 got underway on Tuesday at Arena Grand Paris, with major upsets, thrilling finishes and several strong European performances.

The home crowd had plenty to celebrate as Toma Junior Popov defeated world number one Kunlavut Vitidsarn 9-21, 21-14, 21-15, securing his first career victory over a world number one.

"It's good to win against the world number one. It's my first time, so it's kind of a personal victory for me," Popov said.

Later, he teamed up with his brother Christo Popov to defeat India's Satwiksairaj Rankireddy/Chirag Shetty 21-19, 18-21, 21-7, also claiming their first victory over the Indian pair.

France's reigning world champions Thom Gicquel/Delphine Delrue made a convincing start, defeating England's Callum Hemming/Estelle van Leeuwen 21-14, 21-12.

Denmark's Daniel Lundgaard/Mads Vestergaard survived one of the day's most dramatic encounters, winning 21-18, 30-29 against Lee Jhe-Huei/Yang Po-Hsuan (TPE), with a fortunate net cord deciding the final point.

Mia Blichfeldt advanced after defeating reigning European champion Kirsty Gilmour 21-9, 24-22, while Spain's Ruben Garcia/Lucia Rodriguez also progressed following a three-game victory.

Meanwhile, Christian Faust Kjær/Rasmus Kjær suffered a narrow three-game defeat against Malaysia's Goh Sze Fei/Nur Izzuddin.

Elsewhere, Indonesia's 19-year-old Moh. Zaki Ubaidillah caused another major upset, defeating fourth seed Jonatan Christie 16-21, 21-17, 21-17.

The first-round action continues on Wednesday, with more exciting matches expected in Paris.

beIN Asia Pacific secures exclusive Wimbledon broadcast rights across SEA, Hong Kong until 2031
article_text:
Singapore — beIN Asia Pacific has secured exclusive broadcast rights to The Championships, Wimbledon across Southeast Asia and Hong Kong from 2027 to 2031, expanding its partnership with The All England Lawn Tennis Club (AELTC) and bringing live coverage of the tournament to more fans across the region.

Under the agreement, viewers in Brunei, Cambodia, Timor-Leste, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand will be able to watch Wimbledon exclusively on beIN SPORTS and beIN SPORTS Connect from 2027.

The deal strengthens beIN SPORTS’ tennis offering in Asia and builds on the recent extension of its Wimbledon broadcast rights across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) until 2030.

Mike Kerr, Managing Director of beIN Asia Pacific, said the agreement would help the broadcaster deepen its connection with tennis fans and grow its audience across the region.

“Wimbledon is one of the most prestigious and historic sporting events in the world. It transcends tennis. It’s a cultural moment, and we’re proud to bring The Championships exclusively to audiences across Southeast Asia and Hong Kong,” said Kerr.

“This agreement reflects our long-term commitment to the sport and our shared ambition with the AELTC to build on Wimbledon’s strong connection with audiences here, deepen engagement across the region, and drive the next phase of growth together,” Kerr concluded.

Paul Davies, Associate Director, Broadcast, Production and Media Rights at the All England Club, said, “We are absolutely delighted to extend our long-standing partnership with beIN MEDIA GROUP, building on years of exceptional coverage of The Championships across France and MENA. Welcoming Southeast Asia and Hong Kong to beIN’s portfolio marks an exciting new chapter in our relationship.”

“By leveraging the strength of beIN’s premium linear channels and advanced digital platforms, we look forward to deepening fan engagement, growing audiences, and bringing the unique magic of Wimbledon to more tennis fans across Asia than ever before,” added Davies.

The agreement further strengthens beIN SPORTS’ international tennis portfolio, complementing its exclusive rights to all four Grand Slams in MENA and its exclusive Wimbledon coverage in France.

Through the expanded rights deal, beIN Asia Pacific and the AELTC aim to grow Wimbledon’s audience across Southeast Asia and Hong Kong, using live sports coverage and digital platforms to connect more fans with one of tennis’s most recognised tournaments.

title: Italy star Tommaso Menoncello stood down with immediate effect
article_text:
Tommaso Menoncello is set to miss Italy’s Nations Championship campaign after suffering a shoulder injury against Exeter Chiefs.

The Toulouse centre went off in the 43rd minute of Sunday’s 43-40 Champions Cup win. He suffered a sprain in his left shoulder, which is expected to keep him out for several weeks.

It means Menoncello is likely to miss Italy’s autumn games.

It is another setback for the 24-year-old, who joined Toulouse over the summer. He picked up an injury in their first Top 14 game against La Rochelle before returning to action against Castres in early October.

Toulouse are also without Thomas Ramos and Julien Marchand. Both players are doubts for the November Tests. Ramos has been out since early October and is due to undergo more tests.

Menoncello is one of the brightest young talents in world rugby. He was named Six Nations Player of the Championship in 2024 after a series of fine displays for Italy.

Italy enjoyed a strong Six Nations campaign this year, beating both Scotland and England. However, they lost all three of their summer games against Japan, New Zealand and Australia.

Head coach Gonzalo Quesada must now prepare for the autumn without one of his key players. Italy will be keen to climb the table and avoid finishing bottom of their group.

The team that finishes last in the northern hemisphere group will face the bottom side from the southern hemisphere group. The match will decide who takes the overall wooden spoon.

Italy face a tough run of games this autumn. They will play South Africa, Argentina and Fiji before travelling to London for the Nations Championship Finals Weekend.

Menoncello is the latest big name to face a spell on the sidelines. His injury adds to growing concerns over player welfare and the demands of an increasingly busy rugby calendar.

The Nations Championship is almost here, but some big names will miss out.

England, Ireland, France and New Zealand have all been hit by injuries.

Here are five stars who are either ruled out or facing a race to get fit.

France face a huge blow ahead of their November Tests.

Thomas Ramos has suffered a setback with a thigh injury.

The Toulouse star is a key man for France. His skill, pace and goal-kicking make him hard to replace.

He is now expected to miss the autumn Tests, leaving France with a big gap to fill.

Ireland will be without captain Caelan Doris this autumn.

The Leinster star hurt his foot in June. He also had knee surgery, but his recovery has not gone to plan.

Doris will miss the Nations Championship as he works his way back to full fitness.

It is a huge blow for Andy Farrell, who must now find a new leader in the back row.

All Blacks star Ruben Love will miss the rest of 2026.

The 25-year-old has an ankle injury and needs surgery.

Love had played through pain for much of the year before the injury got worse.

He will now miss New Zealand's autumn tour of Europe.

His absence leaves the All Blacks short of another key option in the backs.

England flanker Sam Underhill will miss the Nations Championship.

The Bath star tore his biceps during a match against Harlequins in September.

He needed surgery and could be out until January.

It is a cruel blow for the 30-year-old, who has faced a tough run of injuries.

Steve Borthwick must now plan for the autumn without one of his best tacklers.

Ireland have been hit by another injury blow.

Jack Conan hurt his shoulder while scoring a try for Leinster against Clermont.

The 34-year-old had to leave the field and now faces time on the sidelines.

His injury comes at the worst time for Andy Farrell.

With Caelan Doris already out, Ireland could be without two key back-row stars.

Conan has not yet been ruled out of the Nations Championship.

title: DP World Tour announces return of historic national Open
article_text:
Get the latest news, reviews, analysis and opinion, plus unmissable deals and exclusive offers. Please check the box of every email you wish to receive.

The DP World Tour has announced that the Hero Indian Open will return in 2027.

The historic national open, first played in 1964, will be part of the DP World Tour calendar for the tenth time next year.

First staged in 2015 as part of the Asian Swing, previous winners of the tournament include Matt Wallace and Eugenio Chacarra.

Meanwhile, Alex Fitzpatrick won his maiden DP World Tour victory at the competition earlier this year.

Set to be staged at the Gary Player-designed DLF Golf & Country Club for the eighth time, Hero MotoCorp will once again be the title sponsor.

The event will take place March 18 to 21 2027.

“Their unwavering support to this tournament and unparalleled contribution to global golf are invaluable.

“We look forward to returning to DLF Golf & Country Club for the eighth consecutive time. It is a world-class venue both on and off the course, which provides our players with a true test every year and we are grateful for their continued support and hospitality.

“I would also like to thank the Indian Golf Union (IGU), for their hard work in continuing to develop the game of golf in India. This tournament has played such an important role in their endeavours, and we look forward to another exciting edition in March.”

Having struck a deal with the Asian Tour earlier this year, the DP World Tour will welcome back two national opens in 2027.

The Singapore Open will make a long-awaited return to the DP World Tour in 2027, with Deutsche Bank involved as title sponsor in a deal until 2029.

Meanwhile, the Hong Kong Open will also make a comeback to the calendar, having last featured in 2018, when Aaron Rai came out on top over Matt Fitzpatrick.

Gael Monfils retirement: Paris Masters issues update on potential emotional farewell
article_text:
Paris Masters organisers insist they have “accepted” that Gael Monfils has retired, but they have not completely closed the door on a final appearance from the French magician at this year’s tournament.

Having announced in October 2025 that the 2026 season would be his final year as a professional, Monfils was expected to receive big send-offs at his final two events on home soil, namely the Lyon Open and the Paris Masters.

The former world No 6 received a wildcard entry into this week’s Grand Prix Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes in Lyon, but he later withdrew from the event.

Not long after, it was announced that he had abruptly retired with his name appearing on the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) retired list of players on 5 October with no official announcement coming from the player himself.

Barely a few days later, his wife Elina Svitolina dropped a bombshell as she announced that the couple’s five-year marriage is over, adding more context to his decision to retire.

French paper L’Équipe reported that “tennis suddenly lost all meaning” for Monfils with his marriage ending, adding that the 40-year-old “was no longer able to play. Hence his abrupt decision to remove himself from the anti-doping lists”.

It was widely accepted that Monfils would have received a wildcard entry into the Paris Masters – which runs from 2-8 November at Nanterre – with organisers planning a farewell for one of French tennis’ favourite sons.

But those plans have been shelved following this week’s breaking news.

“For now, we don’t have any more news than that and we respect this difficult time in his life,” Paris Masters Tournament Director Cedric Pioline told AFP.

But that doesn’t mean the door has been completely shut with former player Pioline hinting they will be willing to make last-minute changes should Monfils change his mind.

The former world No 5 added: “We still have a little bit of time, even though the tournament will start soon. We have accepted that he has retired. We will adapt as soon as there is contact.”

Monfils has fond memories of the Paris Masters as he reached back-to-back finals in 2009 and 2010, but lost to Novak Djokovic and Robin Soderling, respectively.

The Frenchman, though, has missed the last three editions of the ATP Masters 1000 tournament while he lost in the first round in 2023. His last win at the Paris Masters was in 2021 when he reached the third round before withdrawing due to injury.

title: BFGoodrich sponsoring German club Schalke 04

Neither Schalke 04 nor BFGoodrich have shared specific details about the partnership within the club’s second-highest sponsorship tier.

title: Frost Bank inks sponsorship deal with Rockets, Comets
article_text:
Frost Bank has advanced its sponsorship package with the Rockets and initiated its first women’s sports deal with the new iteration of the Comets, in a pair of multi-faceted collaborations in and out of Toyota Center.

As part of the agreement, which was handled in-house, Frost becomes the official bank of both teams and a founding partner of the WNBA’s Comets. In addition, Frost will be a presence within both organizations through financial literacy initiatives; through giveaways and fan experiences on “Frost Fridays”; as presenting sponsor of the franchises’ NBA Cup and Commissioner’s Cup games, respectively; and through the launch of a premium Frost Legends Club at Rockets and Comets games.

Frost’s previous arrangement with the Rockets included signage across Toyota Center and community events in the Houston area. But with the Comets returning next season -- as the Sun relocate from Connecticut -- the Tilman Fertitta ownership group was able to turn this into a two-team package deal that also leans into the Comet’s legacy.

The Comets won the first three WNBA championships, and Gretchen Sheirr -- the team’s president of business operations -- purposely mentioned that “the return of the Houston Comets marks a historic moment for our city, our fans, and the future of women’s sports.” Frost doubled down on that.

“As women’s sports continue to gain momentum, our partnership with the Comets and expanded relationship with the Rockets reflects Frost’s continued investment in Houston,” said Frost’s Houston region president Richard Mann.

The community aspect of the deal -- which is of the utmost importance to all sides -- has Frost working with both teams to help Houston residents build financial confidence and reach their fiscal milestones.

title: Men’s Eagles take on Spain for final Nations Cup home game in Cary, NC
article_text:
Kickoff is set for 7:30 PM ET and will be broadcast live on Paramount+ and CBS Sport Network.

Having taken wins in their first two tests, the Eagles enter the final preparation block for their third and final home game, targeting a complete performance to round out their opening Nations Cup campaign. The USA men kicked off the series on Independence Day with a 30-29 victory over Portugal in Denver, followed up with a 31-15 win over Zimbabwe in Charlotte last weekend.

Looking to keep the intensity high for the full 80 minutes, the squad are ready for the challenge against a strong Spanish side.

Mark O'Keeffe steps into the matchday 23, replacing winger Conner Mooneyham, who is sidelined with an injury sustained last week against Zimbabwe.

Kapeli Pifeleti returns to play after a week's rest from injury. Captain Jason Damm moves into the number eight jersey while Brandon Harvey starts in the second row. Paddy Ryan comes back into the fold as flanker opposite Cory Daniel.

Chicago Hounds front-row Charlie Abel is set to make his international debut off the bench for the Eagles, injecting an extra power boost alongside the Eagles reserves.

The Eagles currently sit 2 spots ahead of 16th ranked Spain, who narrowly beat out the USA when the teams last met in Charlotte July 2025.

“Each week presents us with a new growth opportunity as we build toward 2027. Spain is a very good side with an excellent kicking game, dangerous attacking players, and the ability to put pressure on you across the field. Our focus this week is on preparing well, improving the areas we know can be better, and earning the right to perform for 80 minutes. We look forward to another opportunity to represent the USA rugby community.”

Following the first wave of Nations Cup matches, the USA Eagles disperse for two weeks before reentering a new camp in Florida as they prepare for an international friendly against Argentina XV in Fort Lauderdale on August 15th.

Tickets for USA v Argentina XV and this week’s USA v Spain in Cary’s First Horizon Stadium at WakeMed Soccer Park are available at https://eagles.rugby/tickets.

Fans can get closer to the action with USA Eagles Experiences at https://usaeagles-experiences.com or catch every minute of the action live on Paramount+.

title: Former South Africa wonderkid set to switch allegiance to France
article_text:
France are set to include a former South Africa Under-20 international in their Nations Championship squad, despite the fact that he is not yet eligible to represent them on the pitch.

Stade Français centre Jeremy Ward has reportedly been named in Fabien Galthié's 42-man squad, marking his first call-up to the French national team.

According to L'Equipe, Ward has been selected in place of Bordeaux centre Nicolas Depoortere, who is expected to miss out.

The 30-year-old joined Stade Français in 2022 and will complete his five-year residency period in 2027. This means he could become eligible to play for France at next year's Rugby World Cup.

However, Ward will not be able to make his international debut during the upcoming campaign. He is therefore unavailable for France's clash with his country of birth, South Africa, on November 13.

Before moving to Paris, Ward spent his entire professional career in South Africa, representing the Sharks and Southern Kings among other sides.

He also captained South Africa Under-20s at the 2016 World Rugby Under-20 Championship in England.

Ward scored two tries in a 59-19 win over Japan in the opening match and helped the Junior Springboks reach the semi-finals.

South Africa were beaten by England in the last four before losing to Argentina in the third-place play-off, leaving them fourth in the tournament.

Ward's inclusion in the squad will give Galthié a chance to assess the centre during training and observe how he fits into the group.

This could help the France head coach decide whether he has a future role to play ahead of the 2027 World Cup.

Speaking to RMC Sport last week about the possibility of one day representing Les Bleus, Ward said: "I think it's a bit difficult because I was part of the under-20 team, I'm capped.

"And in the centres of the French national team, there are a lot of players, some very, very good players. I'm not going to say that if I change my sporting nationality, I'll be in the team, that's not the case. But if an opportunity comes up, maybe."

Rassie Erasmus has plenty of big calls to make ahead of the Nations Championship. But who would make your starting XV?

Take charge of the Springboks and pick your dream team. Choose your 15 players and see how your selections compare with other fans.

title: Former England star set for Ireland switch ahead of Nations Championship
article_text:
Andy Farrell could name former England international Kieran Brookes in his Ireland squad for the Nations Championship when it is announced later today.

Ireland are set to face Argentina, Fiji and South Africa at the Aviva Stadium before travelling to London for the Finals Weekend at Allianz Stadium.

Farrell’s side will be aiming to arrive as the highest-ranked team in the Northern Hemisphere, which would secure them a place in the inaugural final.

They have put themselves in a strong position after winning two of their three summer matches.

However, Ireland may need three victories from three, including against reigning world champions South Africa, to finish top of the standings.

One player who could come into contention is 36-year-old prop Brookes, who recently joined Munster.

The former England international ended his contract with Top 14 outfit Perpignan a year early to move to the Irish province, opening the door to a potential change of international allegiance.

Brookes has already made four appearances for Munster this season and has impressed with his performances, strengthening his case for a possible call-up.

Born in England, he previously represented Ireland at several age-grade levels, including under-18, under-19 and under-20.

He went on to feature for England at senior level, earning selection for their 2015 Rugby World Cup squad before making appearances during the 2016 Six Nations.

After returning from injury, Brookes was part of the squad that secured the Grand Slam.

His last England appearance came in 2016, meaning he has long since served the stand-down period required under World Rugby regulations to switch international allegiance.

Interestingly, Brookes began his rugby career as a hooker before switching to prop. He has also previously named Ireland legend Keith Wood as his rugby hero.

Farrell was part of England’s coaching staff during Brookes’ time in the international set-up, so the Ireland head coach will already be familiar with the front-rower. A reunion could now be on the cards.

Should he win selection, Brookes would join a relatively rare group of players to have represented both England and Ireland at senior international level, despite the number of players who have been eligible to play for both countries over the years.

You're in charge of Ireland! Who makes your starting XV?

Pick your best team from the players available and see how your choices compare with other fans.

Make your selections, build your dream XV and have your say!

title: Tennis | ATP Brussels 2026 | Fearnley brushes aside Gaston to set Chidekh second round clash
article_text:
BRUSSELS, BELGIUM – Jacob Fearnley cruised past Hugo Gaston in straight sets to set up a second round meeting with Clement Chidekh.

A big win for Jacob Fearnley over Hugo Gaston means he is into the second round in Brussels where Clement Chidekh now awaits.

Fearnley will aim to serve aggressively in what is a tricky opening round match against Chidekh.

Despite not having the best record on other surfaces, Chidekh has a tremendous record on indoor hard courts. The Frenchman has won Challenger and ITF events on the surface with Fearnley knowing more than most how much of a threat Chidekh can be with the Frenchman beating the Brit at a Challenger event earlier this season. Now, Chidekh aims to repeat the feat and produce a big win in his season as he has huge aspirations ahead of 2027.

Fearnley will need to serve aggressively and will use the backhand to force errors from Chidekh’s game. Meanwhile, Chidekh will use the forehand to pin Fearnley behind the baseline as he will look to close out rallies at the net. This will be a difficult match for Fearnley and the Brit will need to be at his best level in order to advance to the quarter-finals in Brussels.

title: Hero Indian Open dates announced on 2027 DP World Tour schedule
article_text:
The Hero Indian Open will again feature on the DP World Tour’s global schedule, with the tournament set to take place at the DLF Golf & Country Club in Gurugram, the National Capital Region of Delhi from March 18-21, 2027.

The renowned event will celebrate its tenth edition on golf’s global Tour, having first been staged in 2015, and open the Asian Swing – the third of five Global Swings which form the first phase of the DP World Tour’s 2027 schedule.

The DLF Golf & Country Club, designed by nine-time Major winner Gary Player, will host the Hero Indian Open for the eighth time. The first edition in 2017 saw home favourite S.S.P. Chawrasia claim his second Hero Indian Open title, having been victorious at Delhi Golf Club the year prior, with a seven-shot triumph. In 2023, the venue was named India’s Number One Golf Club at the tenth Annual World Golf Awards.

England’s Alex Fitzpatrick won his maiden DP World Tour victory at the Hero Indian Open earlier this year. A stunning final nine holes at DLF Golf & Country Club - one of the toughest layouts on the DP World Tour - saw him overtake defending champion Eugenio Chacarra.

The 27-year-old joined his elder brother, European Ryder Cup star Matt Fitzpatrick, as a winner on Tour. The siblings made history as the first ever pair to win in successive weeks on the DP World Tour and the PGA Tour.

Hero MotoCorp, the world’s largest manufacturer of motorcycles and scooters for 25 consecutive years, will be the Title Partner of two marquee golf tournaments next season, with the Hero Dubai Desert Classic in January 2027 being the other.

Hero MotoCorp’s relationship with the DP World Tour began in 2015 with the Hero Indian Open. This longstanding association, now entering its second decade is among the longest for any sports event in India and Asia - underpinning Hero MotoCorp’s pivotal role in elevating the tournament's stature to a premier international showcase.

The company has also supported the Hero Challenge - a series of fast-paced showpiece events and short-form social and digital content, as well as the Hero Open, which featured on the DP World Tour schedule from 2020 to 2022. Additionally, Hero MotoCorp’s support extended to the inaugural Hero Cup, a team match play contest that provided European players with valuable experience in the format ahead of the 2023 Ryder Cup.

Ben Cowen, the DP World Tour’s Chief Tournament and Operations Officer, said: "We are grateful for the continued partnership with Hero MotoCorp and Dr. Pawan Munjal on India's National Open. Their unwavering support to this tournament and unparalleled contribution to global golf are invaluable.

“We look forward to returning to DLF Golf & Country Club for the eighth consecutive time. It is a world-class venue both on and off the course, which provides our players with a true test every year and we are grateful for their continued support and hospitality.

“I would also like to thank the Indian Golf Union (IGU), for their hard work in continuing to develop the game of golf in India. This tournament has played such an important role in their endeavours, and we look forward to another exciting edition in March.”

Dr Pawan Munjal, Executive Chairman, Hero MotoCorp, said: “For over two decades, Hero MotoCorp has been integral to the evolution of India’s National Open, helping it grow into a tournament of international standing. More than a celebration of world-class golf, it has become a platform where Indian talent can test itself against the best and earn its place on the global stage.

“As we strengthen our global partnership with the DP World Tour, we see an opportunity to take this journey further - connecting Indian golf more closely with the world and bringing new perspectives, possibilities, and audiences to the game.”

title: Shorts: Hyrox, RFU, M+C Saatchi Sport & Entertainment
article_text:
INTERSPORT has extended its European title partnership with HYROX through 2027, expanding into Ireland and Austria as the sporting goods retailer increases its presence across the growing fitness racing series.

The renewed agreement will see the number of INTERSPORT-supported HYROX events double to six in 2027, with Dublin, Vienna and Maastricht joining existing events in Bordeaux, Hamburg and Stockholm.

The partnership, which began in 2025, forms part of INTERSPORT’s strategy to connect with consumers through participation-led sporting events and community engagement.

Under the expanded agreement, INTERSPORT will maintain its title sponsorship of the existing races while introducing branded activations at the three additional locations.

Ireland represents a new market for the collaboration, with INTERSPORT Elverys supporting HYROX Dublin for the first time in 2027.

Andy Hogg, Head of Marketing and Omnichannel at INTERSPORT International Corporation, said, “What makes this partnership special is that HYROX turns individual ambition into a shared experience. As the sport continues to grow, we have an exciting opportunity to bring INTERSPORT closer to athletes and fitness communities across Europe, supporting them not just on race day, but throughout their training journey.”

Across all six events, INTERSPORT will operate activation spaces showcasing hybrid training products, alongside interactive brand experiences and community activities for competitors and spectators.

The retailer will also use the partnership to engage participants throughout their training journeys, rather than focusing solely on race-day sponsorship.

Anne-Marie Hanly, Marketing Manager at INTERSPORT Elverys, said, “HYROX shares that spirit, and we can’t wait to be official partner to HYROX Dublin in 2027.”

HYROX, founded in Germany in 2017, has developed a standardised competition format combining eight 1km runs with eight functional workout stations. The series now operates across more than 30 countries and six continents.

Its expansion has created opportunities for sports retailers and consumer brands to reach participants through both event sponsorship and training-focused commercial activity.

Moritz Fürste, Co-Founder and Chief Marketing Officer at HYROX, said, “INTERSPORT understands that journey and shares our ambition to bring more people into hybrid racing.”

“Extending this partnership through 2027 and growing it across six European race locations means we can support more of our community with the products, expertise and experiences that help them train with confidence and make race day even more memorable.”

INTERSPORT operates 5,260 specialist stores across 40 countries and reported turnover of €14.1bn in 2025.

The Rugby Football Union has renewed its longstanding commercial partnership with Gilbert, extending a relationship that has seen the rugby equipment manufacturer supply England Rugby for more than a century.

Under the new agreement, Gilbert will continue as an Official Supplier to England Rugby, providing match balls, training equipment and clothing for RFU match officials.

The renewal extends more than 25 years of formal commercial partnership between the organisations, although Gilbert’s association with England Rugby dates back considerably further, with its balls used in England matches for over 100 years.

The RFU has not disclosed the financial terms or precise duration of the agreement, although Gilbert described it as the longest-term commitment in the history of the partnership.

Claudio Borges, Executive Director of Commercial and Marketing at the RFU, said, “Gilbert is a truly famous rugby brand and is engrained in our sport. Having a close relationship between the RFU and Gilbert just makes sense. Our partnership goes back over 25 years, and we are excited that we will continue working together for the foreseeable future.”

Founded in the 1820s, Gilbert has become one of rugby’s most established equipment manufacturers, supplying balls and other products across international competitions, professional clubs and grassroots rugby.

Its commercial portfolio includes relationships with World Rugby, the Guinness Six Nations, European Professional Club Rugby, United Rugby Championship and Gallagher PREM Rugby.

Gilbert has also supplied the match balls for every Rugby World Cup since 1995 and is contracted as a supplier for the 2027 tournament.

Richard Gray, Commercial CEO at Gilbert, said, “For over a century, Gilbert balls have been at the centre of England’s greatest moments – and renewing this commitment for our longest term ever is a privilege we don’t take lightly. The length of our partnership is testament to the quality and trust that Gilbert has built for over 200 years – the reason we are the chosen partner of elite unions and grassroots clubs across the globe.”

The renewed agreement maintains Gilbert’s presence across England Rugby’s playing and officiating operations, continuing one of the sport’s longest-running supplier relationships.

It also reinforces the manufacturer’s commercial association with the English game, from grassroots participation through to international fixtures at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham.

M+C Saatchi Sport & Entertainment London has announced a new Executive Creative Director (ECD) appointment, highlighting the growing importance of creativity across sport, culture and entertainment.

The appointment was revealed through a LinkedIn announcement in which the incoming ECD outlined a vision for creative leadership that draws on experience outside traditional advertising.

The announcement emphasised the opportunities for agencies and brands operating at the intersection of sport, entertainment and popular culture, rather than approaching these sectors as separate disciplines.

In the post, the incoming ECD said, “I didn’t come up through advertising. I came through sport, culture and entertainment and I truly believe the most exciting creative work happens at the intersection of all three.”

The appointment reflects an approach to creative leadership focused on combining expertise from different areas of the marketing and entertainment industries.

M+C Saatchi Sport & Entertainment London works across brand partnerships, sponsorship, communications and creative campaigns, connecting brands with audiences through sport and entertainment.

title: Billy Monger and Toyota launch disability sport YouTube series
Newcastle Red Bulls sign Canada lock Flesch
article_text:
Newcastle Red Bulls have signed Canada forward Mason Flesch until the end of the season.

The 26-year-old - who can play at lock or in the back row - has been capped 26 times by his country.

Flesch scored 10 tries in 11 games for Chicago Hounds, including one in the final as his side overcame California Legion to claim the Major League Rugby title and was named the league's forward of the season for 2026.

Ontario-born Flesch came through the ranks with the Toronto Arrows and made his professional debut in 2021 before winning his first Canada cap later that year.

Head coach Dan McFarland told the Newcastle website:, external "Mason has been a stand-out performer in Major League Rugby and for his country, and deserves this opportunity.

"He is a great athlete who will add depth to a very competitive area of our squad, and I look forward to working with him in our environment."

Flesch, who arrived on Tyneside this week, added: "I'm incredibly excited to be a part of this team.

"I'm looking forward to being involved with a quality full-time organisation, and most importantly very eager to train and help push standards."

Newcastle have lost their first three Prem games this season and also lost their European Challenge Cup opener 47-14 at Scarlets last Saturday.

title: Scotland make front-row decision ahead of third Wallaroos clash
article_text:
Interim Scotland head coach Dave Butcher has made three changes to his starting XV for their final WXV Global Series match against Australia in Canberra this Friday.

Hooker Aicha Sutcliffe will make her first start in a Scotland jersey, lock Sarah Bonar is back in action in the second row after recovering from illness and Chloe Rollie returns to the starting line-up at full-back.

Glasgow Warriors duo of centre Nicole Flynn and tighthead prop Imogen Spence are also set to make their debuts from the bench.

This clash marks a third WXV Global Series Test against the Wallaroos, who claimed a 30-10 victory at the Hive Stadium in September and overpowered them 56-12 at Accor Stadium last week.

Rhona Lloyd and Katie Buchanan, who dotted down for her first try for Scotland against the Wallaroos last week, retain their places on the right and left wings, with Chloe Rollie completing the back three.

Vice-captain Helen Nelson moves to inside centre and is partnered by Meryl Smith on the outside.

Leia Brebner-Holden keeps her place at scrum-half and links up with Hannah Ramsay for the half-back partnership.

In the front row, Anne Young and Elliann Clarke start at loosehead and tighthead prop respectively, alongside Aicha Sutcliffe at hooker.

Holland Bogan partners Bonar in the second row, whilst the back row remains unchanged as captain Rachel Malcolm leads at blindside flanker, with Rachel McLachlan starting on the openside. Evie Gallagher will line up at No. 8 once more.

On the bench, Butcher has opted for a five-three split of forwards and backs, with Lana Skeldon, Leah Bartlett, Hollie Cunningham, Eva Donaldson and potential debutant Spence named as forward replacements, whilst Ceitidh Ainsworth, the uncapped Flynn, and Lucia Scott provide backline cover.

title: Lions release statement on the cause of Hyron Andrews' death
article_text:
The Lions have released a statement explaining the reasons behind the sudden and tragic death of lock forward Hyron Andrews on the eve of his side’s Champions Cup tie against La Rochelle.

It was reported that the 6’8 second-row was found unresponsive at the Lions team hotel on Île de Ré, where the South African side had been staying ahead of Saturday’s fixture.

The match went ahead with his teammates’ blessing, as they wanted to honour the popular 31-year-old. La Rochelle beat the Johannesburg side 31-14.

The Lions Rugby Company statement reads: “Lions Rugby Company, on behalf of the Andrews family, confirms that, following an autopsy report, Hyron’s death was found to be caused by an aortic dissection. This dissection most likely occurred on an aortic aneurysm.

“The French authorities, who conducted the autopsy and, in whose care Hyron’s body currently remains, described the cause of death as “a tear in the aorta (due to natural causes), which led to a significant accumulation of blood within the sac surrounding the heart.”

“The Andrews family asks for respect, privacy and patience during this difficult time as the repatriation process begins.

“A timeline for the return of Hyron’s body to South Africa has not yet been determined. Further information will be communicated when it becomes available and under the guidance of the family.”

title: NIBE becomes Premium Sponsor of the LaVita IBU World Cup and World Championships Biathlon
article_text:
Salzburg, Austria / Markaryd, Sweden – NIBE, a leading provider of energy-efficient and sustainable climate solutions, today announced a new strategic partnership with Infront, the International Biathlon Union's (IBU) exclusive global marketing partner, joining the IBU ecosystem as a Premium Sponsor across the LaVita IBU World Cup, IBU World Championships and LOOP ONE Festival.

Rooted in its Nordic heritage, NIBE has built its business around harnessing renewable energy through intelligent, energy-efficient technology. Its climate solutions, spanning heating, cooling, ventilation and hot water, are designed to reduce energy consumption and carbon emissions from buildings, helping households and businesses move away from fossil fuel-based heating while maintaining a comfortable indoor climate. By leveraging the global reach of biathlon and NIBE's expertise in energy-efficient climate solutions, the collaboration aims to create meaningful connections with fans while promoting a more sustainable future.

NIBE will enjoy a significant presence across the IBU's premier events and platforms. The partnership includes extensive branding and activation rights, featuring venue advertising, start number placements at select locations, rifle stickers, warm-up area branding, press conference and victory ceremony backdrops, stadium advertising, fan activation spaces, hospitality opportunities and VIP experiences. It will also benefit from logo integration across IBU platforms, promotional rights and a range of additional marketing assets designed to maximise engagement both on and off-site.

Maria Hägg, Head of Marketing & Communications at NIBE said: " Partnering with the IBU provides a unique opportunity to engage with passionate winter sports fans who share our appreciation for nature and the environment. At NIBE, we have spent decades developing energy-efficient climate solutions that help reduce energy use and carbon emissions from buildings. Through this partnership, we want to create engaging experiences for fans while raising awareness of the role intelligent, renewable energy technologies can play in the transition to a more sustainable future.”

Michael Witta, Senior Vice President Marketing Sales & Services at Infront commented: "This partnership is a strong example of how leading brands can connect authentically with passionate sports audiences through shared values. NIBE's use of technology to positively counter some of the environmental and sustainability challenges fans have in many of biathlon’s core markets makes it an excellent fit for the IBU. It’s hugely satisfying to facilitate collaborations like these that create value for all parties while creating a better experience for biathlon fans worldwide."

Felix Bitterling, Commercial & Marketing Director of the IBU added: "With NIBE we are welcoming a strong and renowned brand, which is proud of its Nordic heritage, to the Biathlon family. As the IBU works towards reducing biathlon's environmental impact partnering with a company like NIBE is a natural and strategic fit. Together with NIBE’s experience the IBU will further create opportunities to integrate sustainable technology into our event delivery and develop future-oriented solutions. Biathlon provides a great platform and wide visibility to showcase NIBE’s products and ambitions for energy-efficient and sustainable climate solutions.”

NIBE is a leading manufacturer of energy-efficient climate solutions for homes and buildings. Founded in Markaryd, Sweden, NIBE has more than 70 years of experience in combining renewable energy with intelligent technology to create solutions for heating, cooling, ventilation and hot water.

With its roots in Sweden and a presence across international markets, NIBE develops climate solutions designed to reduce energy consumption and carbon emissions while creating comfortable and efficient indoor environments. Through continued innovation and a long-term commitment to quality and sustainability, NIBE is helping drive the transition away from fossil fuel-based heating towards a more energy-efficient, low-carbon future.

title: Lxme takes title sponsorship role as Indian Women’s League eyes growth
article_text:
Lxme, a financial platform designed specifically for women, has become the title sponsor of the Indian Women’s League (IWL).

The deal represents a major move in its dedication to promoting women’s financial independence and generating more opportunities for women to engage, lead, and succeed in various areas of life. The long-term collaboration with Capri Sports demonstrates a mutual conviction that supporting women is not only a social necessity but also a chance to unleash broader economic and societal benefits.

The collaboration unites two organisations focused on a shared objective: establishing an environment where women gain improved access to opportunities, the means to chase their ambitions, and the autonomy to determine success according to their own standards. Although recognising women’s financial empowerment remains essential, women’s sports encounter a comparable issue, as female athletes frequently obtain less visibility, funding, and assistance compared to males.

For Lxme, the partnership is a seamless complement to its objective of empowering women to control their financial destinies. The firm has consistently advocated for the significance of financial autonomy as a way for women to make educated choices, accumulate wealth, and gain control over their lives. With this partnership, Lxme applies that philosophy to women’s sports, acknowledging that providing opportunities for women to engage, compete, and excel is essential to their empowerment.

The collaboration also signifies the first significant sponsorship achievement after Capri Sports’ 15-year dedication to Indian women’s football, highlighting the need for ongoing investment to develop a more robust ecosystem for the sport.

Ms. Jinisha Sharma, Director & Promoter, Capri Sports, said, “We’ve always believed that women’s sport is good business. It needs investment, attention, and the same commercial ambition that has helped build successful sporting properties around the world. When we committed to 15 years of building the Indian Women’s League, we did so because we see the potential to create something of real value for clubs, players, fans and brands. Having Lxme come on board so early in that journey is particularly meaningful because they understand this philosophy. They’ve built their own business around recognising and investing in the economic potential of women.”

“For us, this partnership is about much more than a logo on a jersey. It’s about bringing together businesses that are willing to back their convictions and help build the future of women’s football in India.”

Priti Rathi Gupta, Founder of Lxme, said, “At Lxme, we have always believed that women’s financial independence deserves to be taken as seriously as every other aspect of their empowerment. Our mission has been to challenge the notion that women’s financial futures can take a backseat. We see a similar need in sport, where women athletes continue to deserve greater visibility, investment and opportunity. Our partnership with Capri Sports is a natural extension of this belief that women’s potential should never be limited by how much space they are given. Whether in finance or on the field, empowering women to take charge, participate and succeed on their own terms creates value that extends far beyond the individual.”

With this collaboration, Lxme and Capri Sports seek to promote the development of women’s football in India and foster a future where female athletes gain enhanced visibility, acknowledgement, and opportunities to fulfil their potential. The company strengthens a wider conviction that when women are provided the chance to thrive, the effects reach beyond individuals to families, communities, and the economy.

For both organisations, the collaboration signifies a commitment to a future in which women’s aspirations are backed not only in theory, but also through concrete chances to engage, lead, and thrive.

title: Ireland Rugby: Mark Sexton to coach Ireland XV against Fiji 'A' in November
article_text:
An Ireland XV selection will meet Fiji A in Cork on 20 November with Ulster attack coach Mark Sexton leading the panel.

It will be the first of three confirmed fixtures for Ireland's second-string outfit this season with games against Chile in Belfast on 12 February and England A in Exeter eight days later.

The Ireland Rugby Football Union [IRFU] said the series forms part of a "renewed focus on developing emerging talent", as well as providing players on the international radar with "valuable match minutes in green".

Sexton will be joined on the coaching ticket by Munster duo Jimmy Duffy and Jared Payne, as well as IRFU performance pathway scrum coach Seamus Toomey.

"These fixtures help bridge the gap between provincial rugby and the senior international squad, allowing players to test themselves against quality opposition while gaining valuable experience in a national team environment," said the IRFU's performance director David Humphreys.

"They also give us an opportunity to assess players, build relationships and develop greater depth across the player pool.

"Matches such as the upcoming one against Fiji 'A' in Cork are a valuable part of that process, challenging players in different ways and helping to ensure we continue to develop a strong group of players capable of competing in green at international level."

title: Edinburgh beat English club hijack efforts to sign Hector Patterson on new contract
article_text:
It is no surprise that the SRU hierarchy, on the recommendation of Performance Director David Nucifora and with backing from Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend, has found the money to offer Edinburgh scrum-half Hector Patterson a contract extension to keep him at the club until the summer of 2028.

The 21-year-old may have played just eight competitive club games, but Edinburgh attack coach Tim Sampson believes he's already good enough for a Scotland call-up.

Anyone who watched Patterson go head-to-head with Scotland's first-choice scrum-half, Ben White, when Edinburgh played Toulon in the Challenge Cup at the weekend will understand why the SRU pushed the boat out to keep him, despite interest from English clubs such as Bath, which tried to hijack the deal.

He may have ended up on the losing side, but Patterson gave us good as he got against White and showed exactly why he's seen as one of Scotland’s brightest prospects.

Patterson revealed contract extension talks began only a week or so before the URC started. The SRU may have been forced into action after hearing interest from top English clubs, but whether they did or not, he made it clear he wanted to stay at The Hive.

“It never crossed my mind to leave here,” said Patterson. “Talks began at the back end of pre-season, and I had a long think about it, and it was an easy answer to stay. There are a lot of opportunities here, and I am ready to go after them. The attacking style that’s been brought in suits the way I want to play. We have a great group of young players coming through, alongside some really experienced guys who lead the squad brilliantly."

The scrum-half, whose dad Derrick is a former Scotland international and one of the best nines of his generation, admitted that after agreeing to sign a new deal, he worried he might get injured and couldn’t celebrate his contract extension with an extended run in the Edinburgh first team.

"I’m happy to get it out of the way and done, so I can sort of focus on my rugby more than anything,’ he said. "I’ve always wanted to play here, and I’ve been really happy with the way things have been going at the start of the season. That said, my contract was definitely on my mind in these first few games as I was just scared of injuries and things like that. I can now just fully focus and knuckle down and hope to keep the nine jersey here”

Of his eight games for Edinburgh, four last season and four this, he has finished on the losing side only twice, one of which was the defeat to Toulon last weekend, and it says a lot about Patterson’s strength of character that he was pleased to see White, the Toulon captain, being named to start against him.

“I was definitely happy to see his name on the teamsheet when it was announced," said Patterson. “I can learn a lot from a guy like him. I expected words from him during the game, but it wasn’t too bad. I would love to follow in his footsteps and do the things he does. It was good to face him, a challenge. His kicking game is one of the best. I would definitely try to copy that, along with my long exits in play. He definitely gets stuck in.”

Patterson thinks hard when asked what the main thing he would take from coming up against White so early in his career, in such a highly pressurised European Challenge Cup match. “ Maybe I felt a bit more confident in myself that I can probably keep up with them boys,’ he said. "Maybe Ben does a bit more on the ball, and I don’t have as much confidence to do that at times. Watching him take quick taps and take the ball at the lineout, I would like to bring that into my game, and I can improve in those areas."

Edinburgh attack coach Tim Sampson, who joined the club in the summer and encourages Patterson to express himself on the park, believes he is good enough for a Scotland call-up, but it remains to be seen whether he will be part of the Nations Championship squad when it is announced on Monday. The player said others had mentioned a possible Scotland call-up, but he was only focused on Edinburgh and their URC match against the Lions at The Hive on Friday.

“We like to reward players who progress in their game,” said Sampson. "Hector is a great club man, and he works hard on his game, on his craft. He's excellent here, pre- and post-training. We're seeing a big shift in his game, and he is a great signing and great story for the club. He's a young, up-and-coming scrum-half. He has plenty of room to grow, and he is on the right track.

“Hector is certainly good enough for international rugby, and there is no doubt he's knocking on the door. A couple of quality nines are ahead of him. It's a big step up, no doubt, but I'm sure Hector would certainly prime himself really well to perform well if he got the opportunity.”

Sampson said he wasn’t surprised other clubs were interested, as his performances, even in Edinburgh's first few games of the season, had been outstanding.

title: Lynagh Cup announced for clash between Queensland Reds and Benetton Rugby
World No. 4 Zhang Shuxian’s points drop to zero with no application, no announcement
article_text:
Zhang Shuxian’s name is no longer in the BWF women’s doubles rankings. Tuesday’s weekly update carried no asterisk, no injury note and no retirement statement. The slot she had held with partner Jia Yifan at No. 4 in the world is simply empty.

The BWF operates a 52-week rolling points system, where every result drops off a year after it was earned. Zhang and Jia have not played since the Asian Games in late September and withdrew in sequence from the Denmark Open and the French Open, which was enough to zero their total once the older points fell away.

Neither Zhang nor the Chinese Badminton Federation has commented. The BWF has not either.

Shi Yuqi, the former men’s singles world No. 1, shut down his season with shoulder and back injuries and formally applied for a protected ranking, preserving his points and his main-draw entry while he rehabilitates for 2027.

That is the standard route for a Chinese player who intends to return. It freezes the points, holds the entry rights, and buys months of recovery time. Zhang filed nothing.

“A world top-five pair just vanishes, their points go straight to zero, and they haven’t even applied for ranking protection, and that action itself speaks louder than any statement.”

Online public notices in China have circulated suggesting Zhang has accepted a sports teaching position at Southwest Minzu University, Sina Sports reports. The screenshot is doing the rounds, but no one in the chain has confirmed it, not the player, not the university, not the federation.

Without a protected ranking, a return would mean starting again at the lower qualifying events and rebuilding her points from scratch, which Sina Sports describes as a steep physical and competitive barrier for a doubles player who turns 27 in January.

The partnership with Jia Yifan reached No. 4 in the world and lifted a second title of the 2026 season at the Australian Open with a 24-22, 21-13 win, according to Sina Sports’ career recap. Zhang’s team haul with China includes Sudirman Cup and Uber Cup gold alongside her titles on the BWF World Tour in women’s doubles.

Jia Yifan has also not entered any BWF event since the Asian Games, and the Chinese federation has not clarified her status.

title: LIV Golfers, DP World Tour Winners And PGA Tour Players' Brother Listed In Second Stage Of Q-School
article_text:
As the DP World Tour heads into its business end of the season, the circuit's Q-School moves to its Second Stage.

Taking place at four different Spanish venues (Fontanals Golf Club, Golf Las Pinaillas, Isla Canela Links and Desert Springs), it provides players with the opportunity to earn their place at the Final Stage in November, where DP World Tour cards will be on the line.

Many high-caliber names have had to endure the pressures of Q-School and, for 2026, a number of notable players are teeing it up in the Second Stage.

From LIV Golfers to former DP World Tour winners, there are lots of recognizable names in the field for the four events, which take place October 29th to November 1st.

Take a look at the big names and which courses they will be tackling below...

Fontanals Golf Club is the first course listed and, looking down the entry list, it has one of the stronger fields of the four tournaments.

Robert Rock is the main standout name, with the Englishman in the field via his position on the DP World Tour Career Money List.

Subscribe to the Golf Monthly newsletter to stay up to date with all the latest tour news, equipment news, reviews, head-to-heads and buyer’s guides from our team of experienced experts.

A two-time DP World Tour winner, Rock is joined by fellow circuit champions Fabrizio Zanotti, Shubhankar Sharma, Tom Lewis, Romain Wattel, George Coetzee and Robert Dinwiddie.

One player to look out for is Jose Luis Ballester, who produced a strong performance during the First Stage to move through to the next stage of qualifying.

A former LIV Golfer, he is one of many players in the Second Stage from the circuit, with the Fireballs GC player earning victory at the PIF Saudi International on the Asian Tour last November.

Ballester is joined by fellow big-hitter, Wilco Nienaber, as well as Dean Greyserman, who is the brother of PGA Tour player, Max.

One last recognizable name in the field is Richard Teder, who came to light when he famously qualified for The Open Championship in 2025 via Final Qualifying. Playing at West Lancashire, the Estonian holed out from 80-yards in a playoff to earn the final spot at Royal Portrush.

In terms of Golf Las Pinaillas, the name to look out for will be LIV Golfer Luis Masaveu who, like Ballester, secured his spot in the Second Stage via First Stage qualifying.

Also a member of Fireballs GC, the 23-year-old has some experience in DP World Tour sanctioned events, with Masaveu previously making starts on the HotelPlanner Tour.

His best result was a T5th at the German Challenge, with the Spaniard looking to make it through to Final Qualifying, which takes place at Infinitum Golf in his home country.

Former DP World Tour winners in the field include Renato Paratore, Yannik Paul, Justin Harding and Alvaro Quiros.

The four men all have victories at some notable tournaments on the top circuits, but have seen their form drop over the last few seasons.

Former Walker Cup player, Tom Sloman, is also in the field, while another name to look out for is Jack Buchanan, who claimed the 2026 Africa Amateur Championship, earning an Open spot in the process.

Several DP World Tour winners are listed in the field at Isla Canela Links, which also includes LIV Golfers Sam Horsfield and Luis Carrera.

Horsfield is a member of Majesticks GC on the LIV Golf League, but injury struggles and poor form in 2026 left the Englishman 57th in the individual standings.

A three-time winner on the DP World Tour, Horsfield will be hoping to earn his place back on the circuit having last teed it up in 2023 at the Dubai Desert Classic.

Joining Horsfield in the field in Huelva, Spain, will be two-time DP World Tour winner, Lucas Bjerregaard.

Earning victories at the Portugal Masters and Alfred Dunhill Links Championship nearly a decade ago, the Dane last played a competitive event in September, missing the cut at the Omega European Masters.

Maximilian Kieffer, Gavin Green, Callum Tarren and Adri Arnaus have wins worldwide and are in the field, while one other name to look out for is Cameron Adam.

The left-handed Scotsman secured his 2026 DP World Tour membership by topping the 2025 Global Amateur Pathway ranking. Adam, though, endured a poor season this year, registering just one top 10 at the Magical Kenya Open.

Desert Springs Resort is the final venue of the four and, as expected, an interesting field will be present in Almeria.

Looking down the entry list, Michael La Sasso is the name that stands out, with the American present after an excellent final round during First Stage bumped him into the qualifying spots.

La Sasso won the final 2026 LIV Golf event in Indianapolis and will be looking to join his LIV counterparts in making it through to Final Qualifying.

Other notable names include DP World Tour winner, Matthew Baldwin, who hit the opening tee shot at this year's Open Championship, which took place at his home club of Royal Birkdale.

Five-time DP World Tour winner, Alex Levy, is in the field having narrowly lost his Tour card a few years ago and failed to get it back.

He is joined by fellow circuit winners in Steven Brown and Gonzalo Fernandez-Castano, who has seven victories on the DP World Tour, the last of which came in 2013.

title: LaLiga president Tebas demands Man City ‘justice’ over Premier League charges
article_text:
LaLiga president Javier Tebas says Manchester City deserve to face “justice” after being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules and has demanded reform at Fifa and Uefa.

Manchester City were found guilty by an independent commission of 114 of the 115 charges levelled against the club for extensive breaches of its cost control rules.

The investigation determined that City worked to ‘artificially inflate the club’s revenues and reduce its costs by more than UK£900 million’ between the 2009/10 and 2017/18 seasons, a period in which they won three of their eight Premier League titles. They were also found guilty of failing to cooperate during the investigation.

The club successfully appealed a ban from European competition handed down by Uefa in 2020 after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled some of the governing body’s allegations could not be punished because of the time elapsed. A €30 million fine was also reduced to €10 million.

However, the Premier League has no such statute of limitations and, should City’s appeal be unsuccessful, the punishment is likely to be much more severe, with points deductions, expulsion and huge financial penalties all among the possibilities.

Several English rivals have suggested they could take legal action against City, whose conduct would also have impacted European clubs – including LaLiga teams – it faced in Champions League competition.

Speaking at the Sportel sports business conference in Monaco, Tebas would not be drawn on specific sanctions but said he had a keen eye on the outcome. He hopes the punishments will be significant enough to act as deterrent to other clubs seeking to bend financial rules in the future.

“Of course, I am interested in Manchester City because in 2017 we participated in [the] Soccerex [conference] in Manchester and the [City] CEO [Ferran Soriano] called me because he was mad at me because I was telling people about all…they were doing,” said Tebas.

“I’m interested in understanding how this story will end. It is important for both the Premier League and the European football ecosystem. There are people who have had to leave Uefa because of Manchester City, so I think we need justice for the Premier League, for Europe and Uefa.”

It is unclear which officials Tebas was referring to, but Yves Leterme, the chief investigator of Uefa’s Club Financial Control Body (CFCB), was singled out for criticism by City in their public statements on the matter. Leterme left Uefa in 2021 but there is no suggestion his departure was linked to City.

When asked by SportsPro whether City’s case highlighted the need for greater financial regulation in European soccer, Tebas noted that LaLiga’s strict spending rules meant its clubs had a fraction of the debts of their European counterparts.

“Of course, we hope the Premier League will understand to be more sensible … they have quite a complicated financial situation,” he said.

Despite his calls for justice on Uefa’s behalf, the typically combative Tebas did not spare European soccer’s governing body, arguing that the sport should be overseen by a wider array of administrative bodies.

Tebas has been a vocal critic of Fifa president Gianni Infantino and his style of management, not to mention his plans to sell a stake in the men’s World Cup.

“I would like to see changes in the governance of Fifa and Uefa and other institutions according to the [rulings] of the sports courts of law,” he elaborated. “We have monopolies and they must be transparent with any decision. This is not happening – not happening.

“We have certain rules and everyone must respect these rules.”
